audience: Sydney accounting, bookkeeping and advisory firm owners, partners and practice managers
buyer: A profitable professional-service firm whose team is doing approved extra work that never reaches the engagement and billing path
observable_moment: A client asks for extra analysis, a manager approves it, the team delivers it and Friday's invoice still reflects the old scope.
commercial_consequence: Unrecovered fees, distorted service-line margin, hidden capacity consumption and an avoidable invoice dispute when the firm tries to recover the work later.
run_lighter_mechanism: Connect client communication, signed scope, the delivery plan and billing so one reviewable scope-change record carries the approved decision through the existing systems.
exception_path: Partners and managers still decide whether to charge, absorb work, protect the relationship, handle urgency or interpret an ambiguous request.
credible_next_action: Bring one signed engagement, one request that expanded the work and the final invoice to an on-site automation review.
problem: Approved out-of-scope work is delivered but does not reliably update the engagement, delivery plan or invoice.
single_message: The system should carry an approved scope decision into delivery and billing; it should not make the commercial decision.
angle: The expensive failure is not recognising extra work. It is letting the decision stop before the invoice path changes.
selected_headline: How do accounting firms stop out-of-scope work becoming unpaid work?
selected_hook: The work was approved. The invoice never changed.
visual_concept: A privacy-safe Sydney professional-services office with a thick terracotta client-work folder physically blocked between an approved scope file and an empty invoice tray.
search_question: How do accounting firms stop out-of-scope work becoming unpaid work?
direct_answer: Give every scope change one controlled path from the client request to the engagement, delivery plan and billing record. Capture what changed, compare it with the signed scope, prepare the fee change and stop routine delivery until the right person approves. Commercial judgement stays human; the handoff should not depend on memory.
promotion_hypothesis: A direct margin consequence and a recognisable client-request moment should be more commercially relevant than generic automation pricing content.
risk_notes: Do not imply that every extra request must be charged
Keep fee and relationship judgement human
Do not invent recovered revenue or client results
